//: Type checking for a JavaScript project (RM-002 R-07 / P2).
There are no .ts files here and there is not meant to be one. The library is
clean ESM with thorough JSDoc; this makes that JSDoc mean something. Run it
with `npm run typecheck`, which uses vue-tsc - a superset of tsc that also
checks SFC templates against their script blocks.
WHY typescript 6 AND NOT 7
TypeScript 7.0 (stable July 2026, Go-native, 8-12x faster) ships no stable
programmatic API until 7.1, so typescript-eslint and the Vue/Svelte/Astro
template checkers cannot run on it. With 29 single-file components, losing
vue-tsc is disqualifying. Revisit when 7.1 restores the API; nothing in this
file will need to change.
OPT-IN, NOT WHOLESALE
`checkJs` is false. A file joins the check by putting `// @ts-check` on its
first line - or, for an SFC, on the first line inside `<script setup>`.
Switching it on globally still reports errors in library code under a parity
freeze, which is not a review anybody can do usefully in one sitting.
THE LEDGER, AND THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT HONEST
RECOUNT, DO NOT INCREMENT. Every number below is produced by a command,
and the command is written next to it. This ledger has now been wrong
twice - A2 found it had drifted since before A1, and RM-004 B3 found it
claiming 53 SFC errors when the tree had 60 and its own itemisation summed
to 61. Both times the cause was the same: somebody edited it instead of
re-deriving it. A ledger whose parts do not add up to its total is a
comment, not a ratchet.

WHAT B3 DID, AND WHAT IT COST
The application tier went to zero: 60 errors, and every SFC now carries the
pragma - so `npm run typecheck` fails on a regression, not just the audit
command. An area that is clean but not opted in is not protected, which is
why the pragma matters more than the count.
11 of the 71 were not type errors at all and were deleted rather than
annotated: 8 `/// <reference path="....ts">` directives in items/ pointing at
pre-migration TypeScript files that do not exist, and 3 `@see <url>` comments
whose angle brackets made the JSDoc unparseable.
Zero suppressions were added. `grep -rn "@ts-ignore\|@ts-expect-error" src`
returns 7 and all 7 are P2s deliberate ones in core/utils.js, each naming the
preserved-bug arity it pins. Seven JSDoc type ASSERTIONS were added, each with
a docblock saying why the narrowing is sound - six of them the same shape,
`event.target` to the input the component itself renders.
STRICTNESS
`strict` is on but `noImplicitAny` is off. That combination is deliberate for
annotated JS: strict null checking is where the real defects are (it is what
found the nullable-controller and the pop()-may-be-undefined cases), while
requiring an explicit type on every parameter of a 2014-era codebase would
bury those under thousands of trivia.
